entries.clue: It may display welcome for person being badly treated (7)

blocks.note: the thing by a front door that often has WELCOME printed on it
someone who lets others walk all over them

annotation.surface: A sign of welcome turns out to be for someone who gets trampled on.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half reads like a shop sign or banner, but it is the literal mat at the front door; the second half is the figurative use.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who is a doormat lets everyone walk over them, just as people wipe their feet on the real thing.

entries.clue: Working sailor lands on Jupiter moon to establish city (7)

indicators.note: the first pieces come down on top of the next, as a down clue is built from the top

blocks.note: on = working, as a machine that is on
tar = sailor
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

annotation.surface: A space sailor touches down on a moon of Jupiter to found a colony.
annotation.walkthrough: Most solvers know Ontario as the Canadian province; the definition is fair because there is also a city of Ontario in California.
annotation.definitionFit: Ontario is a city in southern California, as well as the Canadian province.

entries.clue: Lover representing NATO in central Paris (5)

indicators.note: the letter is swapped for its word in the NATO phonetic alphabet
take the letter at the centre of the word

blocks.note: R is the middle letter of PARIS
the NATO phonetic alphabet word for R

annotation.surface: Some romantic figure stands in for the military alliance in the heart of the French capital.
annotation.walkthrough: The NATO phonetic alphabet (Alpha, Bravo, Charlie…) gives each letter a code word, and R's is Romeo, which also names Shakespeare's lover.
annotation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young hero became a byword, so a romantic suitor is called by his name.

entries.clue: Style of exotic trade supported by business (3,4)

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and altered, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, which holds it up

blocks.note: anagram of TRADE
Co. = company, a business

annotation.surface: A description of the way a foreign trading venture, backed by a firm, is run.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Style of exotic trade' reads as one phrase about commerce, but 'Style' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A named style in design and architecture, the geometric look of the 1920s and 30s.

entries.clue: One who saves initially is against hoarding after disorder (7)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each following word
the first letters come after the piece for disorder

blocks.note: a mess = disorder
first letters of Is Against Hoarding

annotation.surface: A thrifty saver starts squirrelling money away after things get chaotic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One who saves' pulls toward a thrifty person with a piggy bank; the saving here is of souls.
annotation.definitionFit: The Messiah is the promised saviour or deliverer.

entries.clue: You register drug to pick up praise? (6)

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the words are heard rather than read

blocks.note: you + log (register) + E (ecstasy, the drug)

annotation.surface: A question about signing in to collect a prescription, oddly ending on praise.
annotation.walkthrough: E is crossword shorthand for ecstasy. Said quickly, 'you log E' runs together into eulogy.
annotation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech or piece of writing full of praise, often for someone who has died.

entries.clue: Providing support by transferring workers temporarily (9)

blocks.note: backing a motion in a meeting, the sense said SEC-ond
staff seconded to another post are moved there for a spell

annotation.surface: A manager helps out another team by lending them some staff for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: SEC-onding a motion, but se-CONDING an employee.
annotation.definitionFit: To second is both to back a proposal and to move an employee to another post for a time.

entries.clue: It tells broadcaster what to say reporting traffic build-up (7)

definitions.text: It tells broadcaster what to say

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so what follows is heard

blocks.note: a queue of autos (cars)

annotation.surface: A news presenter reading out the traffic report from a prompt.
annotation.walkthrough: Autocue is the British trade name for a teleprompter, the screen a presenter reads from.
annotation.definitionFit: An autocue shows the presenter the script to read on air.

entries.clue: Rehashed leftovers a hit at this high class establishment (4,4,5)

indicators.note: a rehash cooks the ingredients up again in a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A posh hotel's kitchen serves reheated leftovers and the diners love them.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture of rehashed leftovers is ironic: they are the last thing a luxury hotel would admit to serving.
annotation.definitionFit: Hotels are graded by stars, and five is the top rating, so 'high class establishment' describes it.

entries.clue: Something very small splitting Chat Room in half (4)

indicators.note: splitting a word breaks it into two parts, so each of the next two words is cut in the middle
keep one half, here the back half, of each word

blocks.note: second half of CHAT
second half of ROOM

annotation.surface: Something tiny breaking up an online chat room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Something very small splitting' suggests splitting the atom, a nod to the answer itself.
annotation.definitionFit: An atom is the tiny basic unit of matter.

entries.clue: Journey delayed, blocked by idiotic extremists – three times! (10)

definitions.note: triplicate means in three copies; 'three times' is the sense of 'in triplicate'

indicators.note: the piece for delayed is blocked, with something stuck inside it
the extremes, first and last letters, of the word

blocks.note: a trip = a journey
late = delayed
first and last letters of IdiotiC, placed inside LATE to make LA(IC)TE

annotation.surface: An exasperated traveller's train is held up by hotheads, for the third time.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark carries the surface's irritation; the definition is 'three times', as in forms filled out in triplicate. TRIP + LA(IC)TE.
annotation.definitionFit: Something done in triplicate is done three times over.

entries.clue: Rhythmic feel is an essential part of vinyl record (6)

definitions.text: an essential part of vinyl record

blocks.note: the swing or feel of a piece of music

blocks.clueFragment: an essential part of vinyl record
blocks.note: the spiral channel the stylus runs along

annotation.surface: A music fan says rhythm is what makes a vinyl record.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses come from the same music world, so the surface reads as one statement about records.
annotation.definitionFit: A groove is both the swing of a rhythm and the track cut into a record.

entries.clue: Brussels information is about conservative providing dodgy science (8)

indicators.note: the IS goes about, around, the letter for conservative

blocks.note: Brussels is home to the EU institutions
gen = information, British slang
used as is
C = Conservative, placed inside IS to make I(C)S

annotation.surface: A news item about the EU briefing a Tory politician on some shaky research.
annotation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
annotation.definitionFit: Eugenics, the idea of improving humans by selective breeding, is a discredited pseudo-science.

entries.clue: Lecture on ancient defensive structure surrounded by hotels (4,5)

indicators.note: the ancient structure sits inside the hotels

blocks.note: Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H; the first of the two hotels
old (ancient) + fort (defensive structure)
Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H; the second of the two hotels

annotation.surface: A guide lectures about an old castle ringed by hotels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hotels' is plural so it supplies two H's, one each side. Hotel is H in the NATO alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for talking at length, as if giving a lecture nobody asked for.

entries.clue: Conscripts staff for one producing deeds etc. (9)

blocks.note: to draft = to conscript, so conscripts = drafts
to man = to staff

annotation.surface: An army that conscripts soldiers to fill jobs for a legal clerk.
annotation.walkthrough: Both wordplay words are verbs, not the nouns they look like: conscripts means drafts, and staff means man.
annotation.definitionFit: A draftsman drafts documents such as legal deeds.

entries.clue: Speaker chooses line that’s part of picture (5)

indicators.note: what follows is said out loud by a speaker

blocks.note: picks (chooses) + L (line)

annotation.surface: An orator selects a line from a painting.
annotation.walkthrough: L is the standard abbreviation for line, said as its letter name 'el'.
annotation.definitionFit: A pixel is one of the tiny dots that make up a digital picture.

entries.clue: Suggest using spare cash for launch? (5)

blocks.note: to put an idea forward tentatively
the spare change put in a till at the start of trading, the word also meaning to launch a company

annotation.surface: Someone proposes putting surplus money towards a new product launch.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half bundles two more senses: a float is spare change kept in a till, and floating a company launches it on the stock market.
annotation.definitionFit: Float means to put forward an idea, as well as a cash float and launching a firm.

entries.clue: Hero worshipping youth provides name to boss (7)

indicators.note: one letter is given to the word
it is given into the middle of the word for boss

blocks.note: leader = boss
N = name, placed inside the boss word after its third letter

annotation.surface: A young fan of a celebrity gives his name to his manager.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hero worshipping youth' looks like a teenage fan; Hero is the priestess in Greek myth, and Leander the young man who swam the Hellespont nightly to see her.
annotation.definitionFit: Leander was the youth who loved Hero in the Greek legend.

entries.clue: Forcibly enlist group of journalists (5,4)

blocks.note: to force someone into service, as navies once seized sailors
journalists are collectively the press, and a group is a gang

annotation.surface: Reporters being rounded up and made to join up.
annotation.walkthrough: Press gangs once seized men to serve in the navy; the second reading splits it into the press (journalists) as a gang.
annotation.definitionFit: To press-gang someone is to force them into service.

entries.clue: His vote is wasted? No chance (5,2)

indicators.note: wasted as in drunk and all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A cynical voter asks whether his ballot counts, and is told it has no chance.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue: the first part is the wordplay, 'No chance' the curt reply.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Shove it!' is a rude refusal, meaning much the same as 'no chance!'

entries.clue: Turning cool over trip that produces nothing (4,3)

indicators.note: the word for cool is turned round
in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

blocks.note: a fan cools you
a trip = a fall

annotation.surface: A cold spell drawn out over a pointless outing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cool' here is a verb, what a fan does. Naff all is British slang for nothing at all.
annotation.definitionFit: Naff all is British slang for nothing whatsoever.

entries.clue: In the middle, Oscars turned really raunchy (6)

indicators.note: take the middle two letters of each word

blocks.note: middle of osCArs
middle of tuRNed
middle of reALly

annotation.surface: Midway through the Oscars ceremony things got steamy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like a reversal instruction but is only a word to be cored; the indicator covers all three six-letter words.
annotation.definitionFit: Carnal means to do with bodily, sexual desire, so raunchy.

entries.clue: Actor sat in disguise of old style singer (8)

indicators.note: the letters are dressed up in a different arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: An actor posing, disguised as a period singer.
annotation.walkthrough: A castrato was a male singer castrated before puberty to keep a high voice, common in 17th and 18th century opera.
annotation.definitionFit: Castrati were singers of an old, now abandoned, operatic tradition.

entries.clue: Unique attitude aristocrat has no time for (3-3)

indicators.note: T, for time, is removed from both words

blocks.note: tone (attitude) without its T
toff (aristocrat) without its T

annotation.surface: A snob who can't be bothered with a certain kind of manner.
annotation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for an upper-class person. 'Tone' as in tone of voice gives attitude.
annotation.definitionFit: A one-off is something unique, made or happening only once.

entries.clue: Against supporting former partner, a retired criminal (2-3)

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first, holding it up

blocks.note: an ex = former partner
con = against, as in pros and cons

annotation.surface: Someone who opposes backing their former spouse, a retired crook.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in the reverse of their order in the answer, because CON supports EX from below.
annotation.definitionFit: An ex-con is a former convict, one who has retired from crime.

entries.clue: The first gardeners? Some Londoners believe so (4,3,3)

blocks.note: the first couple in Genesis, placed in the Garden of Eden to tend it
Cockney rhyming slang for believe

annotation.surface: A question about who first tended a garden, answered by a nod to Londoners' faith.
annotation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, spoken in East London, swaps a word for a rhyming phrase: 'Would you Adam and Eve it?' means 'would you believe it?'
annotation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve were placed in Eden to tend it, so the first gardeners.

entries.clue: Check top class beverage from India (4)

blocks.note: ch = check, the chess notation
A1 = top class, with the 1 read as I

annotation.surface: An inspector checks a premium drink imported from India.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate, and setters let the digit 1 stand for the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: Chai is spiced tea, the everyday drink of India.

entries.clue: Seafood found around river furrow (7)

indicators.note: the seafood word is found wrapped around the river letter

blocks.note: a winkle is a small edible sea snail
R = river, placed inside the seafood after its first letter

annotation.surface: Shellfish discovered along a riverbank channel.
annotation.walkthrough: Winkles are small sea snails sold at British seaside stalls.
annotation.definitionFit: A wrinkle is a crease or furrow, in skin or cloth.

entries.clue: Like a warm feeling you get next to fire (7)

blocks.note: at = next to, as in 'at the door'
an ingle is a fire in a hearth, as in inglenook

annotation.surface: The cosy glow you feel sitting beside the fire.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the warmth of sitting by a fireside, which is exactly the tingling glow the answer describes.
annotation.definitionFit: Atingle means tingling, as with a warm glow.
